text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Punjab provincial government has decided to levy farm tax on landholdings which it expects will net an annual revenue of about 1.2 billion rupees, sources said.
- Pakistan has refused to reverse its decision not to sign the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty until "threats" to its security from India's nuclear missile programme were removed.

- The Supreme Court issued notices to the President, the caretaker prime minister and the attorney general to submit their replies, within 10 days, to the petition filed by Benazir Bhutto against the dismissal of her government and the dissolution of the National Assembly.
- As manay as 12 people were injured when a powerful bomb exploded in front of a busy shopping mall in the Punjab provincial capital of Lahore.
- The Election Commission decided to hold polls for the national and four provincial assemblies on the same day.
- The International Monetary Fund assured Pakistan it would disburse much needed $160 million in the third week of December.

- The United States asked China not to engage in any nuclear cooperation with Pakistan, although State Department spokesman Nick Burns conceded Washington had no indication that China was violating any agreements on the issue.
- The World Bank is likely to release $200 million to Pakistan for balance of payments support next month, in addition to its annual lending programme, sources said.
- A three-member Pakistani delegation led by Shahid Javed Burki, economic adviser to the prime minister, will arrive in Washington on December 8 for talks with the World Bank and IMF.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan asked banks to create separate subsidiaries to conduct fund management business from January 1, 1997.

- Pakistan will take up the issue of quotas imposed by Western countries on textile imports at next week's ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore, caretaker Commerce Minister Zubair Khan said.
- All state-owned banks have suspended disbursment of loans to the private sector pending fresh instruction from the State (central) Bank of Pakistan, sources said.
